We need to do more practical things, and will we use different software for different customers? Can 3D design really replace physical samples? Today, I want to discuss these questions with you in depth. ## Adapting to 3D Development How should we do it within the company? How to adapt to the 3D development trend? We aim to make our personnel structure more perfect. ### Example of Hugo Boss Let's take a look at the example of Hugo Boss. As a fashion brand, what we really need to do is surprise our customers. Our ambition is to become the premium tech-driven fashion platform in the world, and 3D can help a lot. We have witnessed a huge transformation at Hugo Boss, as we started early with this. The designers, the pattern makers, everyone is working with 3D software. To date, I would say almost four to five hundred people are working with those 3D technologies here on the campus. The transition from classic design and classic methods to this 3D world has been tremendous. ### Benefits of 3D Technology There are heavy benefits of working 3D end-to-end. We have reduced the amount of physical samples needed to create a collection. Teams are becoming much more efficient and, at the end of the day, creating better products. Substance is coming in a very good place, helping us to be better in digital and work faster. We can really explore creation from scratch. Even though I'm not a 3D artist and did not come from a 3D school, I learned everything here on the job. The design idea becomes visual and realistic from the beginning, providing endless possibilities. With a click of a button, I see a color that would usually take months or weeks to ship around the globe. ### Environmental Benefits We have more time to be creative in the design departments, and in the end, it's really good for the environment. A key benefit that we're already seeing today is the ability to use 3D in a consumer-facing manner, creating media and experiences that weren't possible in classical production processes before. ## Collaborative Initiatives A really exciting initiative we've been working on is called Imaginary Ones, where we collaboratively started to build digital products that are super relevant and speak to our consumers. With these new communities emerging, we have the opportunity to do that. This transformation is about witnessing a moment akin to when the internet was created. Every day brings new opportunities and challenges, making it extremely exciting to witness this transformation of the whole industry. It is clear that virtual layers will be omnipresent, changing the way you experience a brand, interact with products, and engage with communities. ## The Importance of Accurate 3D Design We just finished watching Hugo Boss's presentation on the use of 3D virtual technology in combination with their own situation. In fact, they extended from 3D virtual technology to VR, AR, and digital space, as well as the original universe, etc. These prerequisites require us to have very accurate 3D clothing. ### Supply Chain Perspective As a supply chain company, why do we use 3D to develop clothing design? From our regular process, we design, prepare the fabric, prepare the food, review, and finally pass. However, many designers sometimes cannot make choices for their own designs, leading to the production of many rounds of food samples, which significantly increases the cost of sampling. After using 3D technology, we can show these design solutions in 3D in front of us one by one, replacing some of the food samples with 3D clothes. This process makes it very convenient to help designers make their own decisions, ultimately saving a lot of clothes in the early stage. ### Comparison of 3D Designs Some companies may be ahead in 3D design, while others are relatively late. Let's take a look at two 3D comparison pictures. The first is a 3D work made based on a basic understanding of 3D lace fabric. The latter is the effect made after we modified and optimized it. You can clearly see that 3D virtual technology requires in-depth understanding. There is still much to learn, including the material, texture, physical properties of the fabric, and the entire pattern of the clothing, along with some operating settings for rendering. When we accurately use these elements, the correct platform, and the appropriate pattern, we can achieve real 3D design effects. ## Promoting 3D Design How can we promote our 3D design and let customers gain more trust? First, I have prepared a checklist: - Follow the correct 3D design process, known as VQS (Virtual Quality Standard). - Ensure your 3D designer has a solid foundation in technical design to support reasonable testing of your version. If there are issues with the version, it can be difficult for the 3D designer to identify the problems. Our team must have a technical designer (TD) with strong version technology alongside an excellent 3D designer to complete a standard, comprehensive 3D trial process. ### Quality Control As the number of 3D personnel increases, we must have a manager to oversee the quality of the 3D renderings sent to customers. Ensuring consistency and high quality will help gain customer trust and encourage them to interact with us. ### Case Studies Moreover, having sufficient case studies to convince customers is crucial. For example, we have already conducted several trials with customers, reducing costs in multiple rounds. These trials help to increase customer confidence in 3D technology and facilitate its promotion. ## Example of 3D Trials This picture shows a 3D trial we conducted. On the left, we tested the fabric with the CLOUD physical attribute tester, and on the right, we illustrated the effect of the food sample being worn on the platform. If all requirements are satisfied—correct platform, fabric, and version—the 3D trial effect will look impressive. ### Software Integration In the upper right corner, I used Photoshop alongside 3D software. To achieve a more perfect effect, it's often necessary to combine different software, as each has its own advantages. ## Expanding Software Libraries A good 3D effect requires more software to achieve a comprehensive result. For instance, we can use bead embroidery techniques alongside mesh fabrics, leveraging Substance Designer to adjust parameters for each component. As of now, our company has collaborated with many partners to promote 3D virtual technology, including Adobe and Blender. ## Addressing Storage Issues According to McKinsey's fashion status report in 2025, storage problems can significantly affect order situations for supply chain companies. For example, excessive storage may lead brands to reduce their orders the following year. ### Healthy Product Lifecycle Management To address this, we need to create a healthy product lifecycle. Many companies are trying a model of small orders with fast returns. They conduct market tests with initial orders, adjusting strategies based on performance. 3D technology can expedite the production of models that meet customer requirements, allowing for quick generation of small batch test orders. This approach helps to alleviate storage pressures. ## AI and 3D Design Integration Finally, let's talk about the market of AI design. AI and 3D can also be combined effectively. This significantly aids in promotions and e-commerce displays. Additionally, AI-generated style pictures can reduce the time needed for designers to create drawings. ## Conclusion I hope everyone can embrace digitalization and AI to adapt to these technologies for better outcomes. Let's promote 3D technology and AI together, integrating them into our operations and design processes. And that's all I have to say today. Thank you. ```
